name: i-Ready
line: i-Ready is sold to schools. AMP is a complete math curriculum a family can start today.
description: i-Ready Personalized Instruction is sold to schools and covers K–8. AMP is a complete math curriculum families buy directly, through precalculus.
verdict: i-Ready Personalized Instruction for Mathematics is a school program: it isn’t sold for home use, and a school’s assessment and teachers decide its lessons [1][2]. AMP is a complete math curriculum a family can start today, from counting to precalculus.
theirs: i-Ready is a family of products from Curriculum Associates. This page compares AMP with i-Ready Personalized Instruction for Mathematics, a supplemental digital program [1]. Curriculum Associates also sells separate core mathematics and print products.

Personalized Instruction is guided by the results of the i-Ready Inform assessment. Those results assign each student a path of lessons, and teachers can assign lessons of their own. Schools use its reports beside classroom teaching [1][3].
Its purchasing page says Personalized Instruction is not sold for homeschool or private-home use [2].
credit: One system for a school: the assessment, the lessons it assigns and the reports [1][3].
Teachers can assign lessons that fit what the class is studying [1].
Lessons adjust their support while a student works [1].

reasons.title: A family can buy it
reasons.body: i-Ready Personalized Instruction is not sold for home use [2]. A parent creates an AMP learner and practice begins the same day.

reasons.title: It keeps going after grade 8
reasons.body: i-Ready lists Personalized Instruction content for kindergarten through grade 8 [1]. AMP runs from counting through precalculus in one program.

reasons.title: Every next problem is chosen from the last one
reasons.body: i-Ready sets a lesson path from an assessment, and a teacher can assign lessons [1]. AMP chooses each next problem from what the learner just did, and brings learned skills back for review.

reasons.title: It works on your schedule, with paper when you want it
reasons.body: School access to i-Ready follows a teacher’s assignments. AMP is yours at home, with a lesson and a worked explanation at every problem and printable workbooks made for each learner.

theirs: Curriculum Associates describes Personalized Instruction and the Inform assessment on its own pages [1][3]. This comparison makes no claim about studies of i-Ready.
ours: AMP’s research report sets out each part of the program and the published research behind it. It is AMP’s ESSA Tier 4 rationale, and the studies it plans are pre-registered and published whatever the result.

rows.buyers: Schools. Not sold for homeschool or private-home use [2].
rows.range: Personalized Instruction: kindergarten through grade 8. The Inform assessment: K–12 [1][3].
rows.next: A lesson path set from assessment results, and lessons a teacher assigns [1].
rows.adult: A teacher assigns lessons and reads the reports [1].

them: Your school already uses it, and its lessons follow the school’s assessment.
You are a school that wants the assessment, the instruction and the reports from one company.
amp: You want math at home that you can start and manage yourself.
You need a curriculum that continues into high school mathematics.
You want printable workbooks and an explanation at every problem.

questions.question: Is this comparison about every i-Ready math product?
questions.answer: No. It is about i-Ready Personalized Instruction for Mathematics and the assessment that guides it [1][3]. Curriculum Associates also sells separate core mathematics and print products.

questions.question: Can I buy i-Ready Personalized Instruction for home use?
questions.answer: Its purchasing page says it is not sold for homeschool or private-home use [2]. AMP is sold directly to families.

questions.question: My child uses i-Ready at school. Can we use AMP at home too?
questions.answer: Yes. AMP is a separate home routine: create a learner and begin practice on your own schedule.

sources.title: i-Ready Personalized Instruction for Mathematics (Curriculum Associates)
